I start heating up the pan at a slightly higher heat than I normally would use, butter the outside of the bread, put the cheese in the middle, finish assembling, put it on a plate and then pop it into the microwave for 10 to 15 seconds.

It's critical to watch it carefully. The cheese needs to start melting, but you have to stop the microwave before it screws up the bread. Add just a bit of extra butter to the pan (I use a non-stick pan, too), slide the sandwich into the pan, get it all toasty, flip. One large 4-5lb chuck roast, one packet ranch dressing mix, one stick real butter, 5-10 whole mild peppers, or a half cup sliced mild peppers, 5-7 peeled garlic cloves.  

Place half of the garlic on the bottom of a slow cooker. 

Put the roast on top of the garlic. Searing or browning the meat prior to cooking is unnecessary, but some people go the extra step. 

Sprinkle the roast with the entire packet of dressing mix. You can dump it entirely on the top of the meat, or season both sides. Your choice. 

Top the roast with the peppers and the rest of the garlic.

Place the entire stick of butter on top of the meat and peppers. No need to cut the butter into chunks. Just be decadent and plop it on there.

Cover with a lid and cook for 6-8 hours on medium heat. No additional liquid is necessary as the roast will produce its own. The meat is ready when it can be easily pulled apart with forks and browns just a bit. It's especially delicious if you give it a bit of time under the broiler to brown and crisp it just a touch after it's been pulled apart into chunks. 

By the way, the heat from the mild peppers is extremely mild.
